title: SUPERTET 2026 Top 120 English Crackdown Questions Level 1

sections.title: English Language, Grammar, Vocabulary, Comprehension & Pedagogy

questions.question: Had the committee been informed earlier, it ___ a different course of action.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: past unreal condition + would have + past participle.

en.question: Had the committee been informed earlier, it ___ a different course of action.
en.explanation: Third conditional: past unreal condition + would have + past participle.

questions.question: No sooner ___ the bell rung than the students rushed out.
questions.explanation: The fixed inversion is 'No sooner had ... than ...'.

en.question: No sooner ___ the bell rung than the students rushed out.
en.explanation: The fixed inversion is 'No sooner had ... than ...'.

questions.question: The number of applicants who ___ eligible for the scholarship has increased.
questions.explanation: The relative clause refers to plural 'applicants', so 'are' is required.

en.question: The number of applicants who ___ eligible for the scholarship has increased.
en.explanation: The relative clause refers to plural 'applicants', so 'are' is required.

questions.question: It is high time the administration ___ the ambiguity in the rule.
questions.explanation: After 'it is high time', formal English normally uses a past-tense subjunctive-like form.

en.question: It is high time the administration ___ the ambiguity in the rule.
en.explanation: After 'it is high time', formal English normally uses a past-tense subjunctive-like form.

questions.question: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ willing to alter the schedule.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject 'teachers'.

en.question: Neither the principal nor the teachers ___ willing to alter the schedule.
en.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject 'teachers'.

questions.question: The report, together with its appendices, ___ submitted yesterday.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'report' is singular; 'together with' does not change agreement.

en.question: The report, together with its appendices, ___ submitted yesterday.
en.explanation: The head noun 'report' is singular; 'together with' does not change agreement.

questions.question: She is one of those researchers who ___ rarely satisfied with preliminary evidence.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to the plural antecedent 'researchers'.

en.question: She is one of those researchers who ___ rarely satisfied with preliminary evidence.
en.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to the plural antecedent 'researchers'.

questions.question: If I ___ you, I would not interpret the silence as consent.
questions.explanation: The fixed hypothetical form is 'If I were you'.

en.question: If I ___ you, I would not interpret the silence as consent.
en.explanation: The fixed hypothetical form is 'If I were you'.

questions.question: The teacher asked the pupils why they ___ the instruction despite having read it twice.
questions.explanation: The ignoring occurred before the past reporting verb, so past perfect is the clearest sequence.

en.question: The teacher asked the pupils why they ___ the instruction despite having read it twice.
en.explanation: The ignoring occurred before the past reporting verb, so past perfect is the clearest sequence.

questions.question: Scarcely had the lecture begun when the projector ___.
questions.explanation: With 'scarcely had...', the following clause normally takes simple past.

en.question: Scarcely had the lecture begun when the projector ___.
en.explanation: With 'scarcely had...', the following clause normally takes simple past.

questions.question: The committee recommended that the clause ___ removed before publication.
questions.explanation: After recommend that, formal English can use the mandative subjunctive 'be'.

en.question: The committee recommended that the clause ___ removed before publication.
en.explanation: After recommend that, formal English can use the mandative subjunctive 'be'.

questions.question: What the students need most ___ not another worksheet but sustained feedback.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun clause 'What the students need most'.

en.question: What the students need most ___ not another worksheet but sustained feedback.
en.explanation: The subject is the singular noun clause 'What the students need most'.

questions.question: Each of the proposals ___ been examined independently.
questions.explanation: The head of the subject is 'each', which is singular.

en.question: Each of the proposals ___ been examined independently.
en.explanation: The head of the subject is 'each', which is singular.

questions.question: The books that the librarian said had been misplaced ___ eventually found.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'books' is plural, so the main verb is 'were found'.

en.question: The books that the librarian said had been misplaced ___ eventually found.
en.explanation: The head noun 'books' is plural, so the main verb is 'were found'.

questions.question: He would rather the issue ___ discussed privately.
questions.explanation: After 'would rather' for a present/future preference about another person, past tense is conventional.

en.question: He would rather the issue ___ discussed privately.
en.explanation: After 'would rather' for a present/future preference about another person, past tense is conventional.

questions.question: By the time the invigilator arrived, the candidates ___.
questions.explanation: The earlier completed event takes past perfect.

en.question: By the time the invigilator arrived, the candidates ___.
en.explanation: The earlier completed event takes past perfect.

questions.question: The evidence is too ambiguous for any conclusion ___ drawn from it.
questions.explanation: The construction is 'too + adjective + for + noun + to-infinitive'.

en.question: The evidence is too ambiguous for any conclusion ___ drawn from it.
en.explanation: The construction is 'too + adjective + for + noun + to-infinitive'.

questions.question: The principal insisted that every candidate ___ the form in ink.
questions.explanation: Insist that in formal mandative usage takes the base form 'fill'.

en.question: The principal insisted that every candidate ___ the form in ink.
en.explanation: Insist that in formal mandative usage takes the base form 'fill'.

questions.question: Not only the students but also the instructor ___ responsible for the error.
questions.explanation: With not only...but also, agreement commonly follows the nearer subject 'instructor'.

en.question: Not only the students but also the instructor ___ responsible for the error.
en.explanation: With not only...but also, agreement commonly follows the nearer subject 'instructor'.

questions.question: The lecture was so abstruse that only a handful of students could make ___ of it.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'make sense of something'.

en.question: The lecture was so abstruse that only a handful of students could make ___ of it.
en.explanation: The idiom is 'make sense of something'.

questions.question: She objected to ___ treated as though she had no prior experience.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'to' here is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

en.question: She objected to ___ treated as though she had no prior experience.
en.explanation: The preposition 'to' here is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

questions.question: The candidate, as well as his two assistants, ___ expected to attend.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the main subject plural.

en.question: The candidate, as well as his two assistants, ___ expected to attend.
en.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the main subject plural.

questions.question: Were the instructions ___, fewer candidates would make the same error.
questions.explanation: This is an inverted second conditional: Were + subject + comparative adjective.

en.question: Were the instructions ___, fewer candidates would make the same error.
en.explanation: This is an inverted second conditional: Were + subject + comparative adjective.

questions.question: The teacher had the students ___ the paragraph before discussing it.
questions.explanation: Causative 'have + object + bare infinitive' is used for an instructed action.

en.question: The teacher had the students ___ the paragraph before discussing it.
en.explanation: Causative 'have + object + bare infinitive' is used for an instructed action.

questions.question: I would have preferred that you ___ me beforehand.
questions.explanation: For a past unreal preference/regret, 'would have preferred' can take past perfect.

en.question: I would have preferred that you ___ me beforehand.
en.explanation: For a past unreal preference/regret, 'would have preferred' can take past perfect.

questions.question: Hardly had she entered the room ___ the lights went out.
questions.explanation: The standard correlative is 'hardly/scarcely...when'.

en.question: Hardly had she entered the room ___ the lights went out.
en.explanation: The standard correlative is 'hardly/scarcely...when'.

questions.question: The more carefully the rubric is designed, ___ the assessment becomes.
questions.explanation: Correlative comparative construction: the more..., the more....

en.question: The more carefully the rubric is designed, ___ the assessment becomes.
en.explanation: Correlative comparative construction: the more..., the more....

questions.question: There is little doubt that the findings ___ replicated under controlled conditions.
questions.explanation: 'Can be replicated' correctly combines modal + passive infinitive.

en.question: There is little doubt that the findings ___ replicated under controlled conditions.
en.explanation: 'Can be replicated' correctly combines modal + passive infinitive.

questions.question: The teacher avoided making the task ___ difficult for novice learners.
questions.explanation: An adverb modifies the adjective 'difficult'.

en.question: The teacher avoided making the task ___ difficult for novice learners.
en.explanation: An adverb modifies the adjective 'difficult'.

questions.question: Neither of the explanations ___ entirely convincing.
questions.explanation: In standard formal English, neither of + plural noun takes singular agreement.

en.question: Neither of the explanations ___ entirely convincing.
en.explanation: In standard formal English, neither of + plural noun takes singular agreement.

questions.question: A series of carefully designed tasks ___ helped reveal the misconception.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'series' is singular.

en.question: A series of carefully designed tasks ___ helped reveal the misconception.
en.explanation: The head noun 'series' is singular.

questions.question: The students were made ___ the passage twice before answering.
questions.explanation: In the passive of 'make + object + bare infinitive', 'to' is restored.

en.question: The students were made ___ the passage twice before answering.
en.explanation: In the passive of 'make + object + bare infinitive', 'to' is restored.

questions.question: The teacher is accustomed to ___ evidence before accepting a claim.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'be accustomed to' takes a noun or gerund.

en.question: The teacher is accustomed to ___ evidence before accepting a claim.
en.explanation: The phrase 'be accustomed to' takes a noun or gerund.

questions.question: The proposal is worth ___ in greater detail before rejection.
questions.explanation: 'Worth' is followed by a gerund.

en.question: The proposal is worth ___ in greater detail before rejection.
en.explanation: 'Worth' is followed by a gerund.

questions.question: So subtle ___ the distinction that several candidates overlooked it.
questions.explanation: Inversion after 'so + adjective' uses auxiliary before subject: 'So subtle was...'.

en.question: So subtle ___ the distinction that several candidates overlooked it.
en.explanation: Inversion after 'so + adjective' uses auxiliary before subject: 'So subtle was...'.

questions.question: The teacher asked whether the pupils had completed the task and ___ they needed help.
questions.explanation: The second indirect alternative question is coordinated with 'whether'.

en.question: The teacher asked whether the pupils had completed the task and ___ they needed help.
en.explanation: The second indirect alternative question is coordinated with 'whether'.

questions.question: No explanation, however plausible, ___ accepted without evidence.
questions.explanation: The singular subject is 'No explanation'.

en.question: No explanation, however plausible, ___ accepted without evidence.
en.explanation: The singular subject is 'No explanation'.

questions.question: The data ___ insufficient to support a causal claim, despite the author's confidence.
questions.explanation: In formal academic English, plural 'data' can take plural agreement.

en.question: The data ___ insufficient to support a causal claim, despite the author's confidence.
en.explanation: In formal academic English, plural 'data' can take plural agreement.

questions.question: The teacher's remarks were intended to clarify, rather than ___, the issue.
questions.explanation: After 'rather than' parallel bare infinitives are used here: clarify rather than complicate.

en.question: The teacher's remarks were intended to clarify, rather than ___, the issue.
en.explanation: After 'rather than' parallel bare infinitives are used here: clarify rather than complicate.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'intransigent' in the context of a negotiation.
questions.explanation: Intransigent means refusing to change a position or compromise.

en.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'intransigent' in the context of a negotiation.
en.explanation: Intransigent means refusing to change a position or compromise.

questions.question: The committee's decision was described as 'equivocal'. Which meaning fits best?
questions.explanation: Equivocal means open to more than one interpretation or deliberately ambiguous.

en.question: The committee's decision was described as 'equivocal'. Which meaning fits best?
en.explanation: Equivocal means open to more than one interpretation or deliberately ambiguous.

questions.question: A 'perfunctory' inspection is one that is:
questions.explanation: Perfunctory means done with minimal effort or interest.

en.question: A 'perfunctory' inspection is one that is:
en.explanation: Perfunctory means done with minimal effort or interest.

questions.question: If a statement is 'cogent', it is:
questions.explanation: Cogent reasoning is clear, relevant, and convincing.

en.question: If a statement is 'cogent', it is:
en.explanation: Cogent reasoning is clear, relevant, and convincing.

questions.question: To 'obviate' a difficulty is to:
options: make it unnecessary or prevent it
questions.explanation: Obviate means remove the need for or prevent something.

en.question: To 'obviate' a difficulty is to:
options: make it unnecessary or prevent it
en.explanation: Obviate means remove the need for or prevent something.

questions.question: A 'fastidious' learner is most likely to be:
options: very attentive to detail and standards
questions.explanation: Fastidious describes meticulous attention to detail.

en.question: A 'fastidious' learner is most likely to be:
options: very attentive to detail and standards
en.explanation: Fastidious describes meticulous attention to detail.

questions.question: The word 'disinterested' most precisely means:
options: unbiased and not seeking personal advantage
questions.explanation: Disinterested means impartial; uninterested means lacking interest.

en.question: The word 'disinterested' most precisely means:
options: unbiased and not seeking personal advantage
en.explanation: Disinterested means impartial; uninterested means lacking interest.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'infer' correctly?
options: The data infer that the hypothesis is false.
The researcher inferred the author's intention from the pattern of omissions.
The teacher inferred the students to revise.
The result was inferred by the table.
questions.explanation: A reader/listener infers something from evidence; evidence itself suggests or implies.

en.question: Which sentence uses 'infer' correctly?
options: The data infer that the hypothesis is false.
The researcher inferred the author's intention from the pattern of omissions.
The teacher inferred the students to revise.
The result was inferred by the table.
en.explanation: A reader/listener infers something from evidence; evidence itself suggests or implies.

questions.question: Choose the most precise word: The witness's account was ___ with the video evidence.
questions.explanation: Congruent means in agreement or harmony with something.

en.question: Choose the most precise word: The witness's account was ___ with the video evidence.
en.explanation: Congruent means in agreement or harmony with something.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly distinguished?
options: complement = praise/add to completeness; compliment = remark of praise
questions.explanation: Complement completes or enhances; compliment expresses praise.

en.question: Which pair is correctly distinguished?
options: complement = praise/add to completeness; compliment = remark of praise
en.explanation: Complement completes or enhances; compliment expresses praise.

questions.question: The idiom 'to read between the lines' means to:
questions.explanation: It means to infer meaning that is not explicitly stated.

en.question: The idiom 'to read between the lines' means to:
en.explanation: It means to infer meaning that is not explicitly stated.

questions.question: If a plan is 'feasible', it is:
questions.explanation: Feasible means capable of being done successfully or practically.

en.question: If a plan is 'feasible', it is:
en.explanation: Feasible means capable of being done successfully or practically.

questions.question: Choose the correct collocation.
questions.explanation: 'Pose a question' is the standard collocation.

en.question: Choose the correct collocation.
en.explanation: 'Pose a question' is the standard collocation.

questions.question: Which sentence is semantically most precise?
options: The policy will affect on attendance.
The policy will effect on attendance.
questions.explanation: Affect is normally the verb meaning influence; effect is usually a noun or a less common verb meaning bring about.

en.question: Which sentence is semantically most precise?
options: The policy will affect on attendance.
The policy will effect on attendance.
en.explanation: Affect is normally the verb meaning influence; effect is usually a noun or a less common verb meaning bring about.

questions.question: Choose the correct use of 'adverse'.
options: The teacher gave an adverse of the poem.
The evidence was adverse to proving anything.
questions.explanation: Adverse commonly means harmful or unfavorable, especially before a noun.

en.question: Choose the correct use of 'adverse'.
options: The teacher gave an adverse of the poem.
The evidence was adverse to proving anything.
en.explanation: Adverse commonly means harmful or unfavorable, especially before a noun.

questions.question: Which option best captures the distinction between 'credible' and 'credulous'?
options: credible = believable; credulous = too ready to believe
questions.explanation: Credible describes something worthy of belief; credulous describes a person too ready to believe.

en.question: Which option best captures the distinction between 'credible' and 'credulous'?
options: credible = believable; credulous = too ready to believe
en.explanation: Credible describes something worthy of belief; credulous describes a person too ready to believe.

questions.question: The phrase 'a red herring' refers to:
questions.explanation: A red herring diverts attention from the relevant issue.

en.question: The phrase 'a red herring' refers to:
en.explanation: A red herring diverts attention from the relevant issue.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word: The speaker's claim was ___ by three independent studies.
questions.explanation: Corroborated means confirmed or supported by additional evidence.

en.question: Choose the most appropriate word: The speaker's claim was ___ by three independent studies.
en.explanation: Corroborated means confirmed or supported by additional evidence.

questions.question: 'Mitigate' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Mitigate means reduce the severity, seriousness, or harmfulness of something.

en.question: 'Mitigate' most nearly means:
en.explanation: Mitigate means reduce the severity, seriousness, or harmfulness of something.

questions.question: Which is the best meaning of 'salient' in an academic passage?
questions.explanation: Salient means prominent or especially relevant.

en.question: Which is the best meaning of 'salient' in an academic passage?
en.explanation: Salient means prominent or especially relevant.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a correctly used phrasal verb?
options: The researcher carried the experiment outly.
The researcher carried out the experiment carefully.
The researcher carried on the experiment out.
The researcher carried the experiment with.
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' means perform or conduct.

en.question: Which sentence contains a correctly used phrasal verb?
options: The researcher carried the experiment outly.
The researcher carried out the experiment carefully.
The researcher carried on the experiment out.
The researcher carried the experiment with.
en.explanation: 'Carry out' means perform or conduct.

questions.question: Choose the correct expression.
options: different to from the two models
questions.explanation: In formal standard English, 'different from' is the safest construction.

en.question: Choose the correct expression.
options: different to from the two models
en.explanation: In formal standard English, 'different from' is the safest construction.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'less' appropriately in formal standard English?
options: There were less candidates this year.
There is less uncertainty in the revised model.
questions.explanation: 'Less' is normally used with uncountable nouns; 'uncertainty' is uncountable.

en.question: Which sentence uses 'less' appropriately in formal standard English?
options: There were less candidates this year.
There is less uncertainty in the revised model.
en.explanation: 'Less' is normally used with uncountable nouns; 'uncertainty' is uncountable.

questions.question: Choose the best completion: The teacher's explanation was clear enough to leave little room ___ misunderstanding.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'room for misunderstanding'.

en.question: Choose the best completion: The teacher's explanation was clear enough to leave little room ___ misunderstanding.
en.explanation: The standard collocation is 'room for misunderstanding'.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
options: After reading the article, the teacher assigned a task.
Walking to school, Riya noticed the rain.
Walking to school, the rain soaked Riya.
Having checked the figures, the researcher revised the table.
questions.explanation: The opening participial phrase must logically modify the subject; rain cannot walk to school.

en.question: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
options: After reading the article, the teacher assigned a task.
Walking to school, Riya noticed the rain.
Walking to school, the rain soaked Riya.
Having checked the figures, the researcher revised the table.
en.explanation: The opening participial phrase must logically modify the subject; rain cannot walk to school.

questions.question: Which sentence is free from ambiguity?
options: I saw the teacher with the telescope.
The teacher told the student that he was late.
After the bell rang, the class began the test.
She discussed the result with the researcher in the room.
questions.explanation: 'After the bell rang...' has a clear grammatical relationship and no competing attachment.

en.question: Which sentence is free from ambiguity?
options: I saw the teacher with the telescope.
The teacher told the student that he was late.
After the bell rang, the class began the test.
She discussed the result with the researcher in the room.
en.explanation: 'After the bell rang...' has a clear grammatical relationship and no competing attachment.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct parallelism.
options: The course aims to develop reading, writing, and to speak.
The course aims at reading, writing, and speaking.
The course aims to develop reading, writing, and speaking.
The course aims developing reading, writing, and speaking.
questions.explanation: The coordinated complements after 'develop' should be parallel gerund forms.

en.question: Select the sentence with correct parallelism.
options: The course aims to develop reading, writing, and to speak.
The course aims at reading, writing, and speaking.
The course aims to develop reading, writing, and speaking.
The course aims developing reading, writing, and speaking.
en.explanation: The coordinated complements after 'develop' should be parallel gerund forms.

questions.question: Choose the correct inversion.
options: Rarely I have seen such precision.
Rarely I saw have such precision.
Rarely have I seen such precision.
Rarely have seen I such precision.
questions.explanation: Negative/restrictive adverbials at the front trigger subject–auxiliary inversion.

en.question: Choose the correct inversion.
options: Rarely I have seen such precision.
Rarely I saw have such precision.
Rarely have I seen such precision.
Rarely have seen I such precision.
en.explanation: Negative/restrictive adverbials at the front trigger subject–auxiliary inversion.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'only' to mean that the students, not the teacher, submitted the forms?
options: The students submitted only the forms.
The students only submitted the forms.
Only the students submitted the forms.
The students submitted the forms only.
questions.explanation: Placing 'only' before 'the students' limits the subject.

en.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'only' to mean that the students, not the teacher, submitted the forms?
options: The students submitted only the forms.
The students only submitted the forms.
Only the students submitted the forms.
The students submitted the forms only.
en.explanation: Placing 'only' before 'the students' limits the subject.

questions.question: Choose the sentence in which the pronoun reference is clearest.
options: When Anita spoke to Neha, she looked worried.
Anita told Neha that she was worried.
When Anita spoke to Neha, Anita looked worried.
The teacher told the parent that she should wait.
questions.explanation: Repeating the noun removes the ambiguous pronoun reference.

en.question: Choose the sentence in which the pronoun reference is clearest.
options: When Anita spoke to Neha, she looked worried.
Anita told Neha that she was worried.
When Anita spoke to Neha, Anita looked worried.
The teacher told the parent that she should wait.
en.explanation: Repeating the noun removes the ambiguous pronoun reference.

questions.question: Which option best preserves the meaning: 'Despite being tired, he continued teaching.'
options: He continued teaching so that he was tired.
Because he was tired, he stopped teaching.
Although he was tired, he continued teaching.
He was tired unless he continued teaching.
questions.explanation: Although + clause expresses the same concessive relationship.

en.question: Which option best preserves the meaning: 'Despite being tired, he continued teaching.'
options: He continued teaching so that he was tired.
Because he was tired, he stopped teaching.
Although he was tired, he continued teaching.
He was tired unless he continued teaching.
en.explanation: Although + clause expresses the same concessive relationship.

questions.question: Choose the best word: The conclusion is ___ on an assumption that has not been tested.
questions.explanation: Predicated on means based on.

en.question: Choose the best word: The conclusion is ___ on an assumption that has not been tested.
en.explanation: Predicated on means based on.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'hardly'?
options: Hardly I had arrived when it started.
Hardly did I arrived when it started.
Hardly had I arrived when it started.
Hardly had I arrive than it started.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had + subject + V3 + when' is the standard inverted construction.

en.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'hardly'?
options: Hardly I had arrived when it started.
Hardly did I arrived when it started.
Hardly had I arrived when it started.
Hardly had I arrive than it started.
en.explanation: 'Hardly had + subject + V3 + when' is the standard inverted construction.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: He was appointed ___ honorary adviser to the committee.
questions.explanation: 'Honorary' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

en.question: Choose the correct article: He was appointed ___ honorary adviser to the committee.
en.explanation: 'Honorary' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: She has ___ unique ability to detect subtle errors.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' begins with /juː/, a consonant sound, so 'a' is correct.

en.question: Choose the correct article: She has ___ unique ability to detect subtle errors.
en.explanation: 'Unique' begins with /juː/, a consonant sound, so 'a' is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: Students who submit late may lose marks.
The book, that I bought yesterday, is useful.
My sister, who teaches English, lives in Lucknow.
The teacher which arrived late apologised.
questions.explanation: A non-defining clause is set off by commas and cannot use 'that' in standard formal usage.

en.question: Which sentence correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: Students who submit late may lose marks.
The book, that I bought yesterday, is useful.
My sister, who teaches English, lives in Lucknow.
The teacher which arrived late apologised.
en.explanation: A non-defining clause is set off by commas and cannot use 'that' in standard formal usage.

questions.question: Choose the best correction: 'He is senior than me.'
options: He is more senior than me only.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'senior' conventionally takes 'to', not 'than'.

en.question: Choose the best correction: 'He is senior than me.'
options: He is more senior than me only.
en.explanation: The adjective 'senior' conventionally takes 'to', not 'than'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'used to' for a past habit?
options: She was used to teach here.
questions.explanation: 'Used to + base verb' expresses a past habit or state.

en.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'used to' for a past habit?
options: She was used to teach here.
en.explanation: 'Used to + base verb' expresses a past habit or state.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'would' for a repeated past action?
options: We would visit our grandparents now every summer.
Every summer, we would have visited our grandparents yesterday.
Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.
We would to visit our grandparents.
questions.explanation: Would can describe repeated past actions when the past time frame is established.

en.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'would' for a repeated past action?
options: We would visit our grandparents now every summer.
Every summer, we would have visited our grandparents yesterday.
Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.
We would to visit our grandparents.
en.explanation: Would can describe repeated past actions when the past time frame is established.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: The teacher suggested that the students ___ their sources.
questions.explanation: Suggest that takes the base form in mandative subjunctive usage.

en.question: Choose the correct form: The teacher suggested that the students ___ their sources.
en.explanation: Suggest that takes the base form in mandative subjunctive usage.

questions.question: Which sentence best avoids a semantic contradiction?
options: The evidence was conclusive but completely uncertain.
The sample was small, so the estimate should be interpreted cautiously.
questions.explanation: The fourth sentence is internally coherent; the others contain contradictory combinations.

en.question: Which sentence best avoids a semantic contradiction?
options: The evidence was conclusive but completely uncertain.
The sample was small, so the estimate should be interpreted cautiously.
en.explanation: The fourth sentence is internally coherent; the others contain contradictory combinations.

questions.question: Choose the most precise preposition: The policy is consistent ___ the stated objective.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'consistent with'.

en.question: Choose the most precise preposition: The policy is consistent ___ the stated objective.
en.explanation: The standard collocation is 'consistent with'.

questions.question: Read: 'A classroom can be quiet because students are deeply engaged, or because they are afraid to speak.' What is the most defensible inference?
options: Silence alone is insufficient evidence of engagement.
questions.explanation: The contrast shows that identical outward behaviour can have different underlying causes.

en.question: Read: 'A classroom can be quiet because students are deeply engaged, or because they are afraid to speak.' What is the most defensible inference?
